accent-mark.context: A wide sideways V accent wedge above a filled note head. Use it for articulation, dynamics and emphasis in music theory lessons and notation tools.

arpeggio-mark.context: A vertical wavy line beside a stack of three chord notes sharing one stem. It stands for a rolled or broken chord in notation and in piano or harp lessons.

tremolo-mark.context: A note stem crossed by three slanted slashes above a note head. It marks rapid repetition of a note in a score and in music theory teaching.

music-staff.context: Five evenly spaced horizontal lines closed by a short barline at each end. It is the ruled staff that notes are written on, used for notation apps, lessons and score editors.

grand-staff.context: Two staves joined by a curly brace on the left and a barline on the right. It is the layout used for piano and other keyboard music with a treble and a bass stave.

chord-diagram.context: A guitar chord chart with three strings, a top nut, two frets and three finger dots. Use it for chord finders, guitar lessons and songbooks.

sheet-music.context: A page of printed music with a title line and a pair of beamed notes. Use it for scores, song files, music libraries and downloads of arrangements.

circle-of-fifths.context: A ring divided into twelve segments around a centre dot, the wheel that maps keys and their relations. Use it for music theory guides, key finders and songwriting tools.

piano-roll.context: A sequencer grid with a small keyboard strip on the left and horizontal note bars of different lengths. Use it for MIDI editors, beat making and music production software.

music-composition.context: A quill pen writing a note onto a staff line. Use it for songwriting, composing and notation editing features.

songbook.context: A closed book with a music note on its cover and a ribbon bookmark hanging from the bottom. Use it for hymnals, fake books, song collections and lesson books.

lyrics.context: Lines of song text with a small music note in the top corner. Use it for lyric views, karaoke text, subtitles in players and song pages.

music-stand.context: A folding music stand with a sheet resting on its ledge, a central pole and tripod legs. Use it for rehearsals, practice sessions, orchestra and lesson scheduling.

conductor-baton.context: A thin conductor's baton with a pear-shaped cork handle, lying on the diagonal. Use it for orchestras, choirs, tempo and conducting content.

guitar-pick.context: A rounded triangular guitar pick with three small grip dots. Use it for guitar shops, gear lists and strumming or plucking topics.

capo.context: A guitar capo clamped across the neck with strings running above and below it. Use it for chord transposing tools, guitar gear and lesson content.

guitar-case.context: A hard case shaped like a guitar, with two latch bars on its front. Use it for instrument travel, gig bags, shipping and music shop categories.

violin-case.context: A tapered violin case lying flat, with a carry handle, a seam and two latches. Use it for string instrument travel, lessons and orchestra gear.

brass-mouthpiece.context: A brass mouthpiece with a wide rim, a deep cup and a tapering shank. Use it for trumpet, trombone and horn gear and brass band topics.

trumpet-mute.context: A long straight mute cone with two cork strips, lying on the diagonal. Use it for brass practice, jazz and orchestra accessory lists.

guitar-tuner.context: A clip-on tuner with a round needle display above a clamp. Use it for tuning, guitar setup and pitch checking features.

patch-cable.context: An audio patch cable with a straight jack plug at each end and a looped cord. Use it for connecting instruments, pedalboards and studio gear.

midi-connector.context: The round face of a five pin DIN plug with a key notch and pins in an arc. Use it for MIDI cables, synth ports and hardware connection settings.

condenser-microphone.context: A large studio microphone with a mesh capsule held inside a round shock-mount ring and a short stand. Use it for recording, podcasting and voice-over topics.

shotgun-microphone.context: A long tube microphone with slotted sides and a pistol grip, lying on the diagonal. Use it for film sets, video production and field audio.

lavalier-microphone.context: A tiny clip-on microphone capsule with a clothing clip and a looping cable. Use it for presenters, interviews, video calls and wireless systems.

boom-microphone.context: A microphone in a shaggy windscreen on the end of a long boom pole, lying on the diagonal. Use it for film sets, news crews and location sound.

gooseneck-microphone.context: A microphone on a long bendy gooseneck rising from a small base. Use it for podiums, conference tables, announcements and broadcast desks.

mic-boom-arm.context: A desk boom arm clamped to a table, with a bent arm carrying a microphone. Use it for podcast and streaming setups and broadcast studios.

pop-filter.context: A round mesh pop filter screen on a bendy arm, placed in front of a microphone. Use it for vocal recording, podcasting and studio gear lists.

microphone-windscreen.context: A handheld microphone whose head is covered by a shaggy foam windscreen. Use it for outdoor interviews, reporting and field recording.

vocal-booth.context: A curved reflection shield behind a microphone on a stand. Use it for voice-over rooms, isolation shields and recording studios.

acoustic-panel.context: A square acoustic foam panel showing two rows of wedges. Use it for soundproofing, studio treatment and room acoustics topics.

on-air-sign.context: A rounded lit studio sign with a broadcast dot and waves, hung by two short mounts. Use it for live broadcasting, recording in progress and podcast studios.

audio-interface.context: A small audio interface box with two input jacks, a small gain knob and a large volume knob. Use it for home studio gear, recording setups and sound card settings.

dj-controller.context: A wide DJ controller with two jogwheels at the sides and a fader between them. Use it for DJ gear, club nights, mixing software and live sets.

effects-pedal.context: A guitar stompbox pedal with two knobs, a small light and a round footswitch. Use it for guitar gear, pedalboards and effects categories.

wah-pedal.context: A wah pedal seen from the side with a hinged sloping treadle on a low base. Use it for guitar effects, expression pedals and volume control.

guitar-amplifier.context: A combo guitar amplifier with a row of knobs along the top and a round speaker grille. Use it for guitar gear, practice rooms and stage setups.

amp-stack.context: An amplifier head sitting on a speaker cabinet with four round speakers. Use it for rock gigs, stage backline and heavy amplification topics.

pa-speaker.context: A trapezoid PA speaker cabinet on a tripod pole stand. Use it for live sound, parties, events and public address setups.

stage-monitor-wedge.context: A floor monitor wedge speaker angled upward, with a driver below its sloped face. Use it for stage sound, rehearsal rooms and live band setups.

line-array.context: A line array speaker stack hanging in a gentle curve from a rigging bar. Use it for concerts, festivals and large venue sound systems.

speaker-driver.context: The front of a loudspeaker driver with a square frame, a cone surround and a dust cap. Use it for speaker building, hi-fi parts and audio specs.

record-crate.context: A crate of vinyl records with one square sleeve and a record label standing up behind the front slat. Use it for record shops, digging for vinyl and collections.

vu-meter.context: An analog VU meter window with an arched scale and a needle. Use it for audio levels, mixing consoles and recording gear.

field-recorder.context: A handheld field recorder with a wide stereo microphone head, a small screen and buttons. Use it for interviews, sound design and portable recording.

audio-knob.context: A rotary audio knob with a pointer line and a row of tick dots around it. Use it for volume, gain and tone controls in audio software and hardware.

audio-fader.context: A vertical mixer fader with a slot track, a rectangular cap and level ticks at the side. Use it for mixing desks, channel levels and volume sliders.

multitrack-audio.context: Three stacked audio tracks, each a row of waveform bars. Use it for multitrack editors, timelines and recording software.

spectrogram.context: A frame filled with dotted columns of different heights, like a heat map of sound over time. Use it for audio analysis and frequency displays.

karaoke.context: A lyric screen with text lines and a microphone in front of its lower corner. Use it for sing-along nights, karaoke bars and lyric display features.

record-needle.context: A tonearm with a small cartridge and a stylus touching the grooves of a record. Use it for turntables, vinyl playback and record player settings.

concert-stage.context: A stage platform with a curtain swept back at each side and a spotlight cone in the middle. Use it for venues, live shows, theatre and event listings.

stage-light.context: A stage light hanging from a bar with a cone of light shining below it. Use it for lighting design, theatre rigs and concert production.

fog-machine.context: A fog machine box blowing a cloud out of its nozzle. Use it for stage effects, parties, haunted houses and theatre production.

setlist.context: A taped sheet with a numbered list of song lines. Use it for gig planning, rehearsal order and playlist editors for bands.

backstage-pass.context: A laminated pass card on a lanyard with a star and a text band. Use it for VIP access, crew badges and event entry.

gold-record.context: A framed vinyl disc with a centre label above a small plaque. Use it for music awards, sales milestones and platinum or gold status.

opera-glasses.context: Opera glasses: two round barrels joined by a bridge on a slim handle. Use it for theatre, ballet, opera and close-up viewing in the audience.

concert-crowd.context: Three fans seen from behind, a taller one in the middle, under a spotlight glow. Use it for audiences, attendance, festivals and live event pages.

busking.context: An open instrument case with coins in it and a guitar standing beside it. Use it for street musicians, tips and donations.

choir.context: Three singers in long robes standing in a row. Use it for choirs, choruses, church music and vocal groups.

disc-jockey.context: A person wearing headphones behind a deck with two platters, hands on the records. Use it for DJs, club nights and party bookings.

ballroom-dancing.context: A dancing couple in a waltz hold, one with a flaring skirt and their hands joined overhead. Use it for dance classes, weddings, balls and partner dancing.

breakdancing.context: A breakdancer upside down, spinning on the head with the legs spread in a V. Use it for hip hop, street dance and dance battles.

flamenco-dancer.context: A dancer with one arm raised high and a long ruffled dress swirling out. Use it for Spanish dance, flamenco shows and cultural events.

hula-dance.context: A dancer in a grass skirt with a flower at the ear and both arms swaying to one side. Use it for Hawaiian culture, luaus and island themes.

indian-classical-dance.context: A dancer in a wide bent-knee stance with one arm out in a hand gesture and a pleated fan skirt. Use it for Indian dance schools, recitals and cultural festivals.

lion-dance.context: The front of a lion dance head costume with big eyes, a horn and a fringe above two legs. Use it for Lunar New Year, parades and Chinese festivals.

audio-balance.context: A horizontal balance slider with the knob centred, a centre tick and arrows to the left and right. Use it for stereo pan and left and right speaker settings.
